literalDefinitions.text: 2. 始点相同的两条射线将平面分成两个区域(图 61).
定义 始点相同的两条射线和以这两条射线为边界的区域的并集，叫做角.
始点相同的两条射线 $OA$ 和 $OB$ 确定两个角. 其中每一个角都叫做角 $AOB$ (或者角 $BOA$)，并记作 $\angle AOB$($\angle BOA$)，射线 $OA$ 和 $OB$ 叫做角 $AOB$ 的边，点 $O$ 叫做角的顶点. 两个角中，我们要讨论的那个角通常在图上用一段弧表示出来.
如果射线 $OA$ 和 $OB$ 不在一条直线上(图 62)，那么以 $OA$ 和 $OB$ 为边的两个角中有一个角是凸角，另一个角不是凸角. 图 62 上，凸角是用一条弧线表示的，非凸角是用两条弧线表示的.
你们知道，当一个角的两边组成一条直线时(图 63)，这个角就叫做平角.

domain.radiusAndLength: A circle has positive radius. Given distance a and radius r are positive in the ordinary construction task; zero-distance degeneracy is separately noted where relevant.
domain.angle: Two boundary rays with a common initial point, plus the selected region. The original explicitly admits convex, nonconvex and straight angles. No convex-only or strictly-interior-point-on-side qualification appears in 368 or 369.
domain.tangency: For tangency to a side ray, the supporting line is tangent and its contact point must belong to that ray, including its initial point. Supporting-line tangency with a foot on the backward extension is not tangency to the side.
domain.triangle: The three sides of a triangle are finite segments, not entire supporting lines. An excircle that contacts two side extensions does not solve 371.

solutions.originalPrompt: 364: 已知圆周$(O,r)$和直线$a$. 如果从直线$a$到点$O$的距离:1) 大于$r$;2) 小于$r$;3) 等于$r$，圆周和直线的相关位置怎样?

subparts.proof: Every point on a is at distance >=h>r from O.
A perpendicular foot H yields intersections at signed distance +/-sqrt(r^2-h^2) from H on a; r^2-h^2>0.
The perpendicular foot has distance r; every other point has larger distance.

solutions.grading: auto is suitable for the three ordered numeric intersection counts [0,2,1]; explanatory names can be in displayAnswer

solutions.originalPrompt: 365. 在已知角$AOB$的两边上分别作出满足下列条件的点:1) 与角的顶点的距离为$a$; 2) 与角$AOB$内部区域里的一点$M$的距离为$a$.

subparts.construction: With center O and radius a, intersect the circle with each side ray. For a>0 there is one point on each distinct ray.
subparts.proof: Points on that circle are exactly those at distance a from O; a ray meets it at parameter a.

subparts.construction: With center M and radius a, take all intersections with each side ray, not all intersections with the full supporting line.
subparts.proof: For ray O+t*u (t>=0, unit u), let q=(M-O).u and h^2=|M-O|^2-q^2. Roots are t=q+/-sqrt(a^2-h^2) when a>=h; retain only nonnegative roots and remove duplicates. This derives every allowed point.

solutions.qualifications: M belongs to the selected angle interior, which may be nonconvex or a straight-angle halfplane. Its perpendicular foot may lie behind O. Thus the supporting-line distance test alone does not determine the number on the ray; each ray can have zero, one, or two intersections. If a=0, the first part collapses to O and the second has no side point since M is interior.
solutions.grading: ungraded; a construction with variable intersections needs a complete method, not one fixed expected answer

solutions.originalPrompt: 366. 已知直线$a$和直线上一点$M$. 求作半径为$r$的圆周，使它和直线$a$相切于点$M$.
solutions.construction: Through M construct the perpendicular to a; mark its two points O1,O2 at distance r from M, one on each side. Draw circles (O1,r),(O2,r).
solutions.proof: The radius OiM is perpendicular to a at its endpoint M, so theorem 35 proves tangency. Conversely theorem 37 forces the center onto this perpendicular and radius r forces exactly those two centers.
solutions.grading: ungraded; displayAnswer must give construction and its justification

solutions.originalPrompt: 367. 过已知圆周上的已知点作这个圆周的切线.
solutions.construction: Join the known center O to the given circle point P; construct the perpendicular to OP through P.
solutions.proof: Theorem 35 proves existence; theorem 37 forces any tangent through P to be this perpendicular, proving uniqueness.
solutions.grading: ungraded; one construction with a reason

solutions.originalPrompt: 368. 1) 求作圆周，使切于已知角的两边.2) 求作圆周，使切于已知角的两边，并通过其中一边上的一个已知点.
solutions.independentDerivation: Put vertex V at the origin and side unit directions u,v. For noncollinear sides, c=u.v lies in (-1,1). Centers equidistant from supporting lines lie on the two bisector lines. For center s(u+v), feet have parameters s(1+c) on both rays, hence s>0 is necessary and sufficient. For center s(u-v), foot parameters are s(1-c) and -s(1-c); one is negative for s!=0, so this other bisector gives no circle tangent to both rays. Radius for the valid center is s*sqrt(1-c^2)>0.

subparts.nonstraight: Choose any center C on the bisector ray of the smaller convex region between the two side rays, excluding V. Drop CH perpendicular to a supporting side; H lies on its ray. Draw (C,CH). Reflection in that bisector makes the other tangent foot lie on the other ray. Infinitely many circles. This is independent of whether the named angle selects the convex or nonconvex region, since the prompt does not require containment in that region.
subparts.straight: The side rays are opposite halves of one line. To have contact belonging to both rays it must be V. Choose any C on the perpendicular through V except V, on either side; draw (C,CV). Both rays are tangent at V. Infinitely many circles.
subparts.warning: Using the bisector ray of a selected nonconvex angle puts both feet on backward extensions and fails; silently excluding straight angles changes the original domain.

subparts.nonstraightNonvertex: If given P is on a side ray and P!=V, the circle passes through P and is tangent to that side, so P is the tangent point. Intersect the perpendicular through P with the smaller-region bisector ray to get C; draw radius CP. The other foot is on the other side ray. Exactly one circle. If VP=t>0 and smaller angle is theta, radius=t*tan(theta/2), with 0<theta<pi.
subparts.nonstraightVertex: If P=V and the sides are noncollinear, no positive-radius circle exists: its radius at V would have to be perpendicular to two nonparallel lines.
subparts.straightNonvertex: If the sides are opposite rays and P!=V, no solution: a common tangency point must be V, and a line tangent at V has no second point of the circle on that line.
subparts.straightVertex: If the angle is straight and P=V, every positive-radius circle centered on the perpendicular through V is a solution. Infinitely many; the two normal directions are both allowed.

solutions.grading: ungraded; both requested constructions, ray qualification, nonconvex interpretation, straight cases and point-at-vertex cases must be correctly stated

solutions.originalPrompt: 369. 求与已知角的两边都相切的圆周的中心的集合.

result.nonstraight: The open bisector ray of the smaller convex region between the two boundary rays. This same locus holds when the specified angle is nonconvex: its own region-bisector ray is opposite and is not the locus.
result.straight: The perpendicular line through the vertex, with the vertex removed, allowing both halfplanes. The two opposite side rays are tangent at their shared vertex.

solutions.proof: Tangency forces equal distances to the supporting lines, giving two bisector lines. Parameterizing centers by s(u+v) or s(u-v) as in 368 and requiring both feet nonnegative leaves only s>0 on u+v. For opposite directions v=-u, the two projection parameters are q and -q; both nonnegative forces q=0, i.e. the normal through the vertex. Positive radius removes the vertex.
solutions.grading: ungraded; geometric locus and explanation, not a single fixed numeric or exact expected token

solutions.originalPrompt: 370. 两个圆周彼此相切于$A$点. 是否存在过$A$点且和这两个圆周相切的直线?
solutions.result: Yes. Exactly one common tangent through A, the perpendicular at A to the line joining their centers.
solutions.proof: For two distinct tangent circles the centers O1,O2 and A are collinear. If A were off the center line, reflection of A in that line would be a second distinct common point, contradicting tangency. Thus the perpendicular through A to the center line is perpendicular to both radii O1A,O2A; theorem 35 makes it tangent to both. Theorem 37 gives uniqueness. Argument covers both external and internal tangency.
solutions.grading: ungraded is appropriate for a reasoned existence question; a displayAnswer cannot stop at yes

solutions.originalPrompt: 371. 求作一圆周，使切于已知三角形的三边.
solutions.construction: Construct two internal angle bisectors; their intersection I lies inside the triangle. Drop ID perpendicular to one side and draw the circle centered I with radius ID.
solutions.proof: The bisector-distance property gives equal distances to all three supporting lines. At vertex A, I is on the internal angle bisector so its equal feet on AB and AC are on their rays; at vertex B the same property places the AB foot on BA. Thus the common AB foot belongs to both opposite endpoint rays and lies on segment AB. Repeat for the other two sides. The radius is positive. Hence the circle is tangent to all three actual segments.
solutions.completeness: For any circle tangent to both segments at a vertex, its center must be on the smaller-region bisector ray as derived in 368/369. Applying this at two triangle vertices forces I, so the incircle is unique. Excircles contact extensions of two sides, not all three segments, and are not additional answers.

solutions.originalPrompt: 372. 点$O(O\in p)$是$p$上与点$A(A\notin p)$最近的点.求证: $(OA)\perp p$.
solutions.proof: Construct the perpendicular from A to p with foot H. If H!=O, triangle AHO is a nondegenerate right triangle with hypotenuse AO, so AO>AH (equivalently AO^2=AH^2+HO^2). But H belongs to p and this contradicts that O minimizes distance from A to p. Hence H=O and (OA) is perpendicular to p. Incidence A not in p prevents a zero-radius/zero-length degeneracy.
solutions.grading: ungraded; complete contradiction proof rather than reasserting the desired theorem
